item.text: {"question_id":"4B.3","answer":"In 2023, legal protections and some corrective actions coexisted with materially inadequate protection in practice. The revised press law guaranteed access to some non-classified public-interest information, but retained prison exposure for press offenses and a bad-faith restriction; the Digital Code criminalized dissemination of false information. [BATCH-0025-E007, BATCH-0025-E011] Authorities detained Shilo FM journalists over reporting on alleged secret jails, arrested or detained Bakuka, Kayiba, and Ngongo Lomango over reporting or criticism, and detained Bujakera over a report he did not author; several were released unconditionally or without charge, but the record does not establish effective remedies or accountability. [BATCH-0025-E011, BATCH-0026-E011, BATCH-0025-E012, BATCH-0025-E013] Journalists were also beaten and detained by soldiers, while RSF described pressure, threats, arrests, disappearances, attacks, self-censorship, an insufficiently independent national broadcaster, and persistent impunity across the information environment. [BATCH-0026-E007, BATCH-0025-E008] Opposition meetings and sit-ins were blocked, demonstrations banned, and opposition figures detained; police violently dispersed the May march, while Tshisekedi praised the police chief who oversaw it. [BATCH-0003-E002, BATCH-0003-E003, BATCH-0002-E011, BATCH-0003-E007] The 30 August Goma operation against a banned protest involved mass killings, injuries, arbitrary arrests, disputed casualty figures, missing persons, delayed and undignified handling of bodies, and flawed proceedings against both civilians and security personnel. [BATCH-0011-E018, BATCH-0011-E020, BATCH-0011-E021] December opposition protests were again prohibited and prevented by police deployment; AP reported physical assaults but could not verify the allegation of live ammunition. [BATCH-0010-E022, BATCH-0021-E009] There were limited favorable or qualifying responses: three officers were detained after the May violence, Diongo was released without charge, journalists were sometimes released, the government condemned some attacks and announced accountability, and police escorted a peaceful October Goma march whose memorandum was received. [BATCH-0002-E012, BATCH-0003-E007, BATCH-0025-E011, BATCH-0026-E007, BATCH-0027-E005, BATCH-0022-E014] The supplied record also reports no government restriction or disruption of internet access in 2023. [BATCH-0011-E011] Overall, the evidence shows recurring restrictions and abuses affecting opposition, protest, journalism, satire, and civic space, with partial and contested remedies rather than reliable protection; most incidents are attributed to state authorities, security forces, provincial officials, or ruling-party/allied supporters, but the passages generally do not establish a personal presidential order.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0003-E002","BATCH-0003-E003","BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0011-E018","BATCH-0011-E020","BATCH-0011-E021","BATCH-0021-E009","BATCH-0025-E008","BATCH-0025-E011","BATCH-0025-E012","BATCH-0026-E007","BATCH-0026-E011"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0022-E014","BATCH-0025-E007","BATCH-0025-E013","BATCH-0027-E005","BATCH-0010-E022"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence is for 2023 and does not establish a personal presidential order for most incidents.","The effectiveness, independence, and final outcomes of most investigations, prosecutions, and announced remedies are unresolved.","Goma casualty figures, responsibility findings, and the completeness of the military proceedings remain disputed or contested; appeals were pending in the supplied account.","Some attacks involved opposition supporters, armed groups, or other non-state actors, so they cannot be attributed wholesale to Tshisekedi's government.","The supplied evidence does not document a nationwide internet shutdown or online-content censorship in 2023, but this does not establish broader protection of civic freedom.","The record does not directly document ruler-specific protection or remedy concerning satire or systematic civil-society monitoring beyond the protest and NGO-registration evidence."],"corrections_made":["Added the omitted Shilo FM detention and release, Bakuka, Kayiba, and Ngongo Lomango cases. [BATCH-0025-E011, BATCH-0026-E011]","Added the broader RSF information-environment findings and the June detention and release of three journalists. [BATCH-0011-E011, BATCH-0025-E011, BATCH-0025-E012]","Preserved attribution limits, non-state-actor involvement, disputed Goma figures, and uncertainty over presidential personal responsibility."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["The answer remains dependent on a supplied 2023 evidence subset and may not capture all relevant civic-society, satire, association, or remedy evidence.","A fuller ledger review would be warranted if later evidence establishes presidential involvement, nationwide patterns, final case outcomes, or independent findings on the effectiveness of investigations and prosecutions."]}
